title: Ants
description: A colony of ants forages for food and lays pheromone trails back to the nest. This is the finished project from the NetTango Builder tutorial.

title: Gas Particle Sandbox
description: Program how gas particles move, collide, and bounce off the walls of a sealed container, then watch the rules play out.

title: Rollypollies
description: Rollypollies wander between a dry chamber and a moist one. Simple movement rules decide where the animals end up gathering.

title: Wolves and Sheep
description: This model explores the stability of predator-prey ecosystems. Such a system is called unstable if it tends to result in extinction for one or more species involved. In contrast, a system is stable if it tends to maintain itself over time, despite fluctuations in population sizes.

title: Sound Propagation
description: A speaker plays sound at different volumes. The greater the movement of the speaker the louder the sound and the greater the amplitude of the particle movement.

title: Thermal Equilibration
description: This model supports a drawing style interface for "sketching" up representations of new systems to explore related to gas behavior and gas particles. This model is part of the "Connected Chemistry" curriculum http://ccl.northwestern.edu/curriculum/ConnectedChemistry/ which explores the behavior of gases.

title: Watermelon Biodiversity
description: Students investigate seedless watermelon (artificial asexual reproduction via grafting) and seeded watermelon (naturally reproducing sexually) to see how they are affected when a fungus is introduced into the population. What can be done to help the watermelons survive the fungus?

title: Fire
description: This project simulates the spread of a fire through a forest. It shows that the fire's chance of reaching the right edge of the forest depends critically on the density of trees. This is an example of a common feature of complex systems, the presence of a non-linear threshold or critical parameter. This model extends the Fire Simple model by adding fire fighting ability.

title: Disease
description: A NetTango blocks environment from the Theory Building collection.

title: Simplified Disease
description: A NetTango blocks environment from the Theory Building collection.

title: Slime Tutorial
description: This model is inspired by the aggregation behavior of slime-mold cells.

title: Wolves and Moose
description: A NetTango blocks environment from the Biology collection.

title: Spaceship Programming
description: Students schedule timed engine firings with blocks to fly a spaceship to a target. The ship keeps its velocity until an opposing engine fires.

title: Spaceship Programming: Variable Engines
description: Follows Spaceship Programming. Students again schedule engine firings with blocks to reach a target, and now set each engine's force from 0 to 10 N.

title: Abstract Exponential
description: Students build rules for wandering particles that hatch new particles by chance each step, and plot how the particle count grows. NetTango version by John Chen. The model file carries the Info text of the NetLogo Models Library model DLA Simple (Wilensky and Rand, 2006) and states a CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 license.

title: Abstract Exponential and Logistic
description: Students build rules for wandering particles that hatch new particles by chance and die when another particle shares their patch, so crowding limits the particle count. NetTango version by John Chen. The model file carries the Info text of the NetLogo Models Library model DLA Simple (Wilensky and Rand, 2006) and states a CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 license.

title: DLA
description: Students build rules for wandering particles that attach to a seed cluster when they touch it, growing branching, treelike structures. NetTango version by John Chen, based on the NetLogo Models Library model DLA Simple (Wilensky and Rand, 2006). Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

title: Preferential Attachment
description: Students build rules for a growing network in which new nodes connect to existing ones, and explore how linking to already popular nodes produces a few highly connected hubs. NetTango version by John Chen, based on the NetLogo Models Library model Preferential Attachment (Wilensky, 2005). Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

title: Rollypollies Simple
description: A NetTango blocks environment from the Biology collection.

title: Free Fall
description: A NetTango blocks environment from the Chemistry and Physics collection.

title: Ideal Gas Law
description: This model enables students to draw a model to "sketch" up representations of new systems to explore concepts related to gas behavior and gas particles. A wide range of real world systems can be modeled with this simple interface (e.g. diffusion of perfume from an uncapped container, hot gas mixed with a cold gas, mixtures of gases).

title: Motion Maps 1D
description: (A graph of position velocity and acceleration for up to 10 cars moving horizontally.)

title: Diffusion Graphics
description: Diffusion Graphics is unlike most other NetLogo models, in that it really doesn't 'model' anything. It simply explores the power behind an interesting patch primitive: 'diffuse'.

title: Antomology - Ant Colony
description: In this game, two colonies of ants forage for food. Though each ant follows a set of simple rules, the colonies as a whole act in sophisticated ways. Ant Adaptation simulates two ant colonies side by side, each controlled by a different player.
